item.title: Nigeria ready to host 126 countries at 2026 PR forum
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has declared its readiness to host the 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF), with representatives from more than 126 countries and leading international institutions expected at the global event scheduled to hold in Abuja from November 15 to 22. The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, gave the assurance at a world press conference in Abuja on Wednesday. The forum, to be hosted under the leadership of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as Chief Host, is expected to bring together global public relations experts, communication professionals, policymakers and representatives of major international organisations to discuss the future of responsible communication. Speaking at the event, Idris described Nigeria’s selection as host as significant recognition of the country’s growing influence in global communication and public relations. He appreciated the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the African Public Relations Association (APRA) for entrusting Nigeria with the responsibility of hosting the international and continental gatherings simultaneously. The minister noted that Nigeria would become the first country in West Africa and the second in Africa to host the World Public Relations Forum, describing the opportunity as a major milestone for the country and the continent. According to him, the forum would provide Nigeria with an important platform to showcase its institutional capacity, strengthen international partnerships and contribute to conversations shaping the global communication industry. With the theme, “Responsible Communication: The Voice of the World,” the 2026 forum is expected to address critical challenges confronting the communication industry, particularly the growing influence of digital platforms, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. Idris warned that the rapid transformation of the information environment had heightened concerns over misinformation, disinformation and the erosion of public trust. He stressed that communication professionals must remain committed to truth, accuracy, transparency and ethical conduct. The minister maintained that the responsibility of public relations practitioners should extend beyond protecting institutional reputations and promoting organisational interests to safeguarding the public interest and ensuring that citizens have access to credible information. He also highlighted the Federal Government’s support for the establishment of the UNESCO Category 2 International Media and Information Literacy Institute (IMILI) in Abuja. He described the initiative as a strategic investment in building an informed society, particularly among young people, by equipping citizens with the knowledge and skills to identify misleading information and navigate the increasingly complex digital environment. item.title: How Do Enterprise Brands Scale TikTok Influencer Marketing?
item.description: Running a TikTok campaign with five creators is manageable. Running campaigns with dozens or hundreds of creators across different products, countries, internal teams, and agencies is a very different challenge. For large brands, the real question is not simply how to find more influencers. It is how to scale TikTok influencer marketing without losing control over creative quality, brand standards, budgets, reporting, and local relevance. That requires systems. Brands need repeatable ways to identify creators, review content, approve campaigns, manage payments, protect the brand, measure results, and learn from previous activity. A specialist TikTok marketing agency can support that process by bringing creator strategy, campaign operations, paid media, and performance measurement into one coordinated structure. The goal is to move from individual creator activations to a repeatable marketing channel. To Scale TikTok Influencer Marketing, Start With the Operating Model Before adding more creators, enterprise brands need to decide how the influencer program will actually operate. Large organizations may have global marketing teams, regional managers, product divisions, legal departments, procurement teams, local agencies, and paid media specialists involved in the same campaign. Without clear ownership, adding more creators can simply add more complexity. Most large influencer programs generally follow one of three models: Centralized: A global team controls strategy, creator selection, budgets, approvals, and reporting. Decentralized: Regional teams manage their own campaigns independently. Hybrid: Central teams establish standards while regional teams control local execution. For multinational brands, the hybrid model can often provide a useful balance. The organization can standardize contracts, reporting, creator-vetting requirements, brand safety, and campaign objectives while allowing regional teams to adapt language, creators, cultural references, and content formats. Vanguard has highlighted the growing importance of having a clear digital strategy rather than simply maintaining a social media presence. Its coverage of why businesses need digital strategy reflects the same principle. Scale should begin with structure, not volume. Standardize What Does Not Need to Change One of the easiest ways for influencer programs to become inefficient is for every campaign to start from zero. Enterprise teams should standardize repeatable processes such as: Creator vetting criteria Campaign brief templates Contract structures Content approval stages Usage rights Disclosure requirements Brand safety checks Reporting definitions Payment processes Performance dashboards This does not mean every campaign should look identical. It means teams should avoid rebuilding the administrative side of the program each time. item.title: CAC, EY warn directors against governance failures
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu The Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) has warned company directors against treating regulatory compliance as the sole responsibility of company secretaries, saying weak corporate records and governance failures could undermine business credibility, investment prospects and access to credit. The Registrar-General and Chief Executive Officer of CAC, Hussaini Ishaq Magaji, gave the warning at the 2026 Audit Committee Transformation Summit organised by Ernst & Young (EY) in Lagos on Wednesday. Magaji said directors’ responsibilities extended beyond strategy, profitability and risk management to protecting the integrity of their companies’ legal identities. He noted that outdated corporate records, undisclosed changes in ownership and failure to file annual returns could expose companies to regulatory sanctions, reputational damage and diminished investor confidence. According to him, “Directors must demonstrate diligence, transparency and accountability by ensuring accurate corporate records, timely statutory filings and proper disclosure of persons with significant control. “The era of filing annual returns as an annual ritual is over. The Corporate Affairs Commission is asking Nigerian boards and companies to move beyond merely filing annual returns towards continuous accountability, transparent ownership, accurate records and credible governance.” He added that companies with transparent ownership structures and disciplined governance would be better positioned to attract investments, secure credit, participate in public procurement and pursue business partnerships. Also speaking, Amina Maida, who represented the Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), said effective audit committees were essential to strengthening corporate resilience amid technological changes, cybersecurity threats and evolving regulatory requirements. She said the NCC issued corporate governance guidelines for the communications industry in 2025, outlining board and committee responsibilities, including risk management, internal controls and audit oversight. In his welcome address, EY Regional Managing Partner, West Africa, Anthony Oputa, said audit committees were performing their oversight responsibilities in an increasingly complex environment shaped by evolving regulatory expectations, geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty, technological disruption, sustainability considerations and significant changes in financial reporting. Oputa, who was represented by Jamiu Olakisan, Assurance Leader, EY West Africa, said the developments were placing greater demands on audit committees to strengthen accounting and internal control systems, enhance corporate transparency, safeguard audit quality and reinforce stakeholder confidence. item.title: Kidnapping: Afenifere seeks sophisticated weapons for Amotekun
item.description: …Demands drones, forest surveillance, grassroots intelligence, full LG autonomy By Adeola Badru The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, has called for a comprehensive overhaul of the South-West’s security architecture, urging governments to equip the Western Nigeria Security Network, codenamed Amotekun, with sophisticated weapons and modern surveillance technology to tackle kidnapping and other violent crimes. The organisation also called for the deployment of drones, improved forest surveillance, coordinated security operations and stronger grassroots intelligence gathering to curb the activities of kidnappers and armed gangs across the region. Afenifere warned that persistent attacks on highways, forests and rural communities exposed gaps in existing security arrangements, insisting that governments must move beyond security meetings and adopt more effective operational strategies. It further cautioned that poverty, educational deprivation and youth unemployment could sustain a recruitment pipeline for bandits and other criminal networks, urging authorities to combine security operations with sustained social and economic interventions. Afenifere’s National Publicity Secretary, Jare Ajayi, made the demands in a statement issued against the backdrop of recent abductions along the Ijebu-Ode–Ibadan highway and at the Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria, FRIN, Ibadan, on Wednesday. The latest incidents included the abduction of travellers heading to Ibadan from Ijebu-Ode, Ogun State, last Tuesday, with their abductors reportedly demanding a ransom of N25 million. One of the victims was identified as Mr Dapo, a recent National Youth Service Corps graduate who had just completed his national service in Edo State. The incident came weeks after prospective corps members travelling from Ibadan were abducted in Imo State on October 1, 2026. Similarly, the kidnapping of victims at FRIN, along the Ibadan–Ijebu-Ode highway, raised fresh concerns, as the location had reportedly witnessed a similar incident a few months earlier. Although the victims were eventually rescued or released, Afenifere said their freedom should not overshadow the recurring nature of the attacks and the threat they posed to residents, commuters and economic activities. Ajayi said, “We are deeply saddened that these disheartening incidents are occurring at all, as they remind us that much still needs to be done to secure the people and ensure their safety.” The organisation described the incidents as part of a disturbing pattern of violent crimes across the Yoruba-speaking states and adjoining areas. It cited the reported beheading of a farmer in Itesiwaju Local Government Area of Oyo State, the kidnapping of Prince Michael Folarin in Igbeti and the abduction of a 33-year-old poultry farmer, Mr Ooreoluwa Osonuga, in Ogun State. item.title: 2027: I’d have joined Rainbow Coalition if still in politics — Ladoja
item.description: By Adeola Badru The Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, has said he would have joined the Rainbow Coalition if he were still active in partisan politics, but noted that his position as a traditional ruler requires him to remain politically neutral. Ladoja said although he appreciated the political initiative behind the coalition, his traditional role demanded fairness, neutrality and equal treatment of all political tendencies, irrespective of party affiliations. The monarch spoke on Wednesday when he received a delegation of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) National Working Committee, led by the party’s National Secretary, Senator Samuel Anyanwu, at his palace in Ibadan. The delegation, which included members of the party’s national leadership and its governorship candidate in Oyo State, Hazeem Gbolarumi, paid homage to the monarch and formally presented the candidate to him ahead of the 2027 general elections. Speaking during the visit, Ladoja said his political disposition would have been different if he were still actively involved in partisan politics. “If I were still a politician, I would have joined the Rainbow Coalition. But now that I am a traditional ruler, my responsibility is different. “I have to accommodate everybody, irrespective of the political party they belong to. I cannot take sides with any political party or candidate. My duty is to receive everybody, advise them and admonish them where necessary,” the monarch said. He stressed that traditional rulers had important roles to play in sustaining democratic stability, particularly during electioneering periods, adding that their influence should be deployed towards promoting peaceful political engagement rather than deepening divisions. The Olubadan also said Nigeria needed a trusted leader capable of commanding public confidence, inspiring national unity and providing purposeful leadership amid the country’s numerous challenges. According to him, the country requires leadership anchored on credibility, integrity and the ability to earn the trust of the people. He urged politicians to place national interest above personal ambitions and partisan considerations, stressing that the political process should be guided by responsibility and genuine commitment to national development. Ladoja also appealed to political stakeholders to conduct themselves in ways that would preserve the peace and stability of the country as preparations for the 2027 general elections gather momentum. Earlier, Anyanwu said the PDP delegation’s visit was part of efforts to sustain the party’s relationship with traditional institutions and seek the monarch’s royal blessings and counsel ahead of the next general elections. He reaffirmed the group’s recognition of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, as the national leader of the PDP, insisting that its political direction remained firmly anchored on the Rainbow Coalition. item.title: ‘Importing wine doesn’t make you an economist’, Tinubu hits Obi, says Atiku has nothing to offer
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure President Bola Tinubu has urged Nigerians to reject opposition presidential candidates, Peter Obi and Atiku Abubakar, in the 2027 general election, saying they have nothing to offer the country. Tinubu, who spoke through Vice-President Kashim Shettima at the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential campaign rally in Akure, Ondo State, described the opposition figures as no match for the President. Shettima challenged Obi and Atiku to present their records in public office and policy alternatives to Nigerians, rather than relying on social media campaigns. He said the opposition had failed to demonstrate what it could offer the country. Shettima takes swipe at Atiku, Obi Shettima questioned Atiku’s political standing in his home state of Adamawa, claiming that even former governors of the state were not supporting him. He also criticised Obi, alleging that his campaign relied on what he described as “obnoxious data” rather than verifiable achievements. “The ability to import cheap South African wines does not make one a guru in economics,” he said. The Vice-President described Obi’s tenure as Anambra State governor as mediocre and challenged opposition politicians to identify their major achievements in the past 25 years of democracy. Ondo leaders rally behind Tinubu Shettima said Tinubu enjoyed what he called a “universal elite consensus” in Ondo State, contrasting it with the alleged lack of support for Obi and Atiku in their respective home states. He cited former Ondo State Governor Olusegun Mimiko, former governorship candidate, Chief Olusola Oke, SAN, and member of the House of Representatives, Gboyega Adefarati, as evidence of the APC’s growing political support in the state. He also claimed that former Anambra governors Chris Ngige, Chinwoke Mbadinuju and Willie Obiano, as well as incumbent Governor Charles Soludo, were not aligned with Obi. Shettima projects 1.2 million votes With Ondo’s registered voters put at 2.1 million, Shettima said the APC was targeting at least 1.2 million votes from the 1.8 million residents said to have collected their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs. He described the turnout at the rally as a political statement, recalling similar outings in Cross River, Nasarawa, Akwa Ibom, Rivers, Ebonyi and Jigawa states. Shettima also contrasted the opposition’s activities with what he described as Tinubu’s achievements in the last three and a half years, while commending Ondo APC leaders for putting their differences aside. Aiyedatiwa promises one million votes In his address, Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa promised to deliver one million votes for Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. Aiyedatiwa thanked the President for what he described as progressive policies and interventions, saying Ondo voted massively for Tinubu in 2023 because of his leadership record as governor of Lagos State. item.title: Apo-Karshi road to become Abuja tourist attraction – Wike
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said the Apo-Karshi road, a project awarded in 2010 but abandoned for years, will be developed into a tourist attraction in Abuja. Wike spoke on Wednesday during an inspection of the completed road in the nation’s capital. He attributed the completion of the project to President Bola Tinubu’s intervention, saying the President ordered the termination of the original contract after the contractor failed to deliver despite receiving full payment. “This road was awarded in 2010 to an indigenous contractor. We did all we could to persuade the contractor to ensure that the job was fully implemented, even though we had fully paid. But the contractor was not forthcoming,” he said. According to the minister, the matter was brought to Tinubu’s attention, following which the President directed that the contract be terminated and re-awarded to a more competent company. Wike said the decision was informed by the strategic importance of the road to residents and the overall development of the FCT. He added that the administration was not deterred by criticism over the cost of the new contract. “When this contract was awarded, some people were asking how we could award it at that amount. But we were not deterred. All we were concerned about was the happiness and comfort of the people,” he said. Wike described the road as one of the most publicised projects undertaken by the Satellite Towns Development Authority (STDA), noting that the difficult terrain made its completion a remarkable engineering achievement. He said reactions on social media showed that many Nigerians were surprised that a project of such scale and engineering complexity could be delivered in the country. The minister also acknowledged journalists for drawing public attention to the project, saying their reports had helped Nigerians appreciate the scale of work carried out on the road. He urged Nigerians to assess the Tinubu administration’s performance holistically rather than judging it based on isolated issues. “Look at what is going on in Abuja today, the level of infrastructure and how it has turned out to be a tourist centre. I am happy that people are happy and that Nigerians have seen the infrastructure development being carried out by the Tinubu administration,” he said. On the commissioning of the road, Wike said the FCT Administration was working around the President’s schedule, as several other projects were also being lined up for inauguration. He expressed hope that Tinubu would inaugurate the Apo-Karshi road before the end of November, adding that efforts would be made to secure a place for the project in the President’s schedule. On plans for public facilities around the road, the minister said the administration would develop appropriate amenities in collaboration with relevant departments. item.title: NULGE slams withholding of Osun LG funds, urges immediate resolution‎
item.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — THE Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE) has condemned the continued withholding of statutory allocations due to local governments in Osun State and called for urgent intervention from the Federal Government and other relevant stakeholders. ‎ ‎The union said the development had deepened the leadership and funding crisis in the state’s local government system, prompting workers to stage a warning strike from Sunday, November 8, to Wednesday, November 11, 2026. ‎ ‎In a statement jointly signed by its President-General, Comrade Aliyu Haruna, and General Secretary, Comrade Gambo Isah, NULGE stressed that local government workers should not suffer the consequences of political disputes, leadership tussles or administrative faentitlement ‎ ‎According to the union, the Supreme Court’s affirmation of local government financial autonomy must go beyond legal recognition and produce real financial independence, improved services, and timely payment of workers’ dues. ‎ ‎It noted that local government autonomy would be of little value without access to funds, cautioning that councils could not function effectively when their finances were withheld and workers’ legitimate entitlements were denied ‎ ‎NULGE consequently “called for the immediate resolution of all outstanding issues surrounding the release and accessibility of funds due to local governments in Osun State.” ‎ ‎It also demanded “an urgent and lasting resolution of the leadership crisis in the state’s local government system in accordance with constitutional and legal provisions.” ‎ ‎The union further urged authorities to protect workers against salary delays, denial of entitlements and victimisation arising from the crisis. ‎ ‎It called on the Federal Government, Osun State Government and other relevant stakeholders to intervene and engage constructively to restore normalcy and industrial harmony in the state. ‎ ‎Expressing solidarity with the leadership and workforce of NULGE in Osun State, the national leadership assured the workers that the union would not abandon its responsibility to defend their rights, welfare and dignity. ‎ ‎While urging the affected workers to remain peaceful and disciplined, NULGE “called on all parties to demonstrate political maturity and genuine commitment to resolving the crisis without further delay.” ‎ ‎The union warned that “the continued withholding of local government funds is not merely a labour issue but also a threat to grassroots democracy, effective service delivery and the economic survival of thousands of Nigerian families.” ‎ ‎It declared that the time for political blame games was over, insisting that decisive action was needed to end the crisis and protect the interests of local government workers across the country. item.title: 2027: Atiku can’t unite Adamawa, let alone Nigeria — Shettima
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Vice-President Kashim Shettima has questioned whether African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar can unite Nigeria, claiming the former Vice-President lacks political consensus in his home state of Adamawa. Shettima made the claim while campaigning for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election at the APC presidential campaign rally in Akure, the Ondo State capital, on Wednesday, setting up a contrast between what he described as weak opposition support in Adamawa and Anambra and the broad backing for the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ondo. The Vice president argued that the political alignments in the three states showed the difference between the opposition’s position and the support Tinubu had gathered for his re-election bid while noting that former vice president Atiku had not secured the backing of any of Adamawa’s five governors since the return to democracy in 1999. “Our political opponents can conduct political rallies on Facebook and on Instagram, but for somebody who cannot build a consensus at the home front, Atiku Abubakar is from Adamawa state. He has been unable to build a lead consensus, even in his own Adamawa State,” Shettima said. “Of all the five governors that have ever ruled Adamawa State in the current dispensation—from Mr. Boni Haruna to Vice Admiral Murtala Hamman-Yero Nyako to Barrister Bala James Ngilari to Senator Muhammadu Umaru Jibrilla (Bindow) to Rt. Hon. Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri—none of these governors and former governors are in alignment with Atiku Abubakar. He also listed prominent politicians in the state whom he said were not aligned with the ADC candidate. “All the political mavericks in Adamawa State, from the former SGF Boss Gidahyelda Mustapha to Engineer Babachir David Lawal, to Senator Aishatu Dahiru Ahmed (Binani), and all the major political actors in Adamawa State, are not in alignment with Atiku.” Shettima also cited the political divisions in Adamawa as evidence, saying they raised questions about Atiku’s ability to unite the country. “And right now, he has three gubernatorial candidates in Adamawa. So someone who cannot unite his own state, I wonder how he is going to unite and drive the nation as a whole,” he said. The Vice president then contrasted his account of the opposition’s support in Adamawa with the turnout for Tinubu in Ondo, describing it as a demonstration of backing for the President’s re-election. “Here in Ondo, Ondo, the game is over. item.title: Reps to probe rising human trafficking, trafficking networks
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has resolved to investigate the rising incidence of human trafficking in Nigeria, mandating its Committees on Human Rights, Interior and Police Affairs to probe the activities of trafficking syndicates and assess the effectiveness of existing measures to combat the crime. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by Rep. Dominic Okafor, titled, “Need to Investigate the Alarming Increase in Human Trafficking in Nigeria”, at Wednesday’s plenary. The lawmakers expressed concern over the growing threat posed by human trafficking, particularly to women, children and other vulnerable groups. The House noted that human trafficking remained a grave violation of human rights and dignity, involving the recruitment, transportation, transfer, harbouring or receipt of persons through force, coercion, deception, abuse of vulnerability or other prohibited means for the purpose of exploitation. It observed that victims were increasingly subjected to commercial sexual exploitation, forced labour, domestic servitude, forced begging, organ harvesting and other forms of degrading abuse. The lawmakers attributed the growing vulnerability of Nigerians to trafficking to poverty, unemployment, insecurity, displacement, irregular migration and the activities of organised criminal networks. They further noted that many victims were lured through false promises of employment, education, marriage and opportunities abroad, only to end up in exploitative conditions characterised by physical abuse, psychological trauma and, in some cases, death. The House also expressed concern that trafficking networks operated across state and international borders, exploiting porous borders, inadequate public awareness, weak coordination among relevant agencies and difficulties in identifying and prosecuting offenders. While acknowledging the efforts of the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Immigration Service and other relevant institutions, the lawmakers stressed the need to strengthen their operational capacity, funding, intelligence-sharing and victim-support mechanisms. The House recalled the provisions of the Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition) Enforcement and Administration Act, 2015, and other relevant legislation aimed at preventing trafficking, prosecuting offenders and protecting victims. Consequently, the lawmakers urged the Federal Government to intensify nationwide efforts to combat human trafficking through effective enforcement of existing laws, intelligence-led investigations and prosecution of traffickers and their collaborators. They also called for improved victim identification, rescue, rehabilitation, psychosocial support, legal assistance and reintegration programmes, particularly for women, children and other vulnerable persons. item.title: Withheld Osun LG fund: National public sector union body backs Osun strike
item.description: *Warns FG of total shutdown By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Umbrella body for public sector union in the country, the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC, Trade Union Side, has thrown its weight behind the three-day warning strike declared by the Osun State Council of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, over the continued withholding of statutory allocations meant for local government areas in the state by the Federal Government. The national leadership of the council described the industrial action as justified, warning that the prolonged withholding of local government funds, which it said had lasted for about 21 months, had inflicted severe economic hardship on local government workers and their dependants. It called on the Federal Government to immediately release the outstanding allocations to prevent an escalation of the industrial dispute. The national body also cautioned that the continued withholding of the funds could undermine grassroots administration and deepen the economic difficulties confronting workers across Osun State, stressing that urgent intervention was necessary to avert a total shutdown. In a statement by the National Secretary of JNPSNC, Gbenga Olowoyo, on behalf of the national leadership, the council said: “The National leadership of Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council JNPSNC (Trade Union Side), under the Chairmanship of Comrade Benjamin Anto Uyanto mni, has thrown its weight behind the current three days strike called by the Osun State Council of the Nigeria Labour Congress NLC over the continued withheld of the Local government fund by the Federal Government. “The JNPSNC reviewed all the circumstances surrounding the reason for the solidarity strike called by the Osun State Council of NLC, which was premised on the urgent need to release the withheld statutory allocation due to local government areas in the state since February 2025, that is now about 21 months of withholding the fund (from February 2025 to November 2026) and considered it as very justifiable. “The National leadership of JNPSNC considered the continued withheld of the Osun State local government fund by the Federal Government is not only excessive use of political power but also reckless without conscience, on account that the far reaching negative implications on the economic fortunes of the local government administration on one hand and the economic subjugation on the local government workers and their dependants on the hand is better imagined than experienced. “Consequent upon the cry of the entire workers in Osun State, it is very desirable for the Federal Government and all concerned to release the fund without further delay in order to allow Osun State local government workers and their dependants to have economic breath. “The National leadership of JNPSNC regretted that under democratic administration the Federal Government and its agencies responsible for the withheld allocations could descend so low to the exten

item.title: Zamfara: Jaji wins APC rerun primary by 26,646 votes
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau A member representing Kaura-Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji, has won the All Progressives Congress (APC) fresh primary election for the constituency with a landslide victory. Jaji emerged winner of the rerun primary conducted on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, polling 26,646 votes to defeat his closest challenger, Hassan Umar Dangaladima, who scored 713 votes. The third aspirant, Musa Zubairu, polled no votes. The Chairman of the APC Electoral Committee for the Kaura-Namoda/Birnin Magaji fresh primary, Hon. Kabiru Idris, announced the results at the constituency’s collation centre in Kaura-Namoda. Giving a breakdown of the exercise, Idris said the constituency had 42,266 registered party members, out of whom 27,389 were accredited to vote, while 27,359 votes were cast. In the results announced, Jaji scored 14,264 votes in Kaura-Namoda Local Government Area, against Dangaladima’s 465 votes, while Zubairu scored zero. In Birnin Magaji Local Government Area, Jaji polled 12,382 votes, while Dangaladima secured 248 votes. Zubairu again scored zero. Declaring the result, Idris said Jaji had satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC constitution and the party’s guidelines, and was therefore returned as the winner of the fresh primary. The rerun followed a suit filed by Dangaladima at the Federal High Court, Abuja, which nullified Jaji’s earlier nomination and ordered the party to conduct a fresh primary within two weeks. The APC national leadership subsequently fixed November 11, 2026, for the rerun, in compliance with the court’s order. item.title: APC chieftain to DSS: Scrutinise Dino Melaye’s statements
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi An All Progressives Congress (APC) chieftain and loyalist of President Bola Tinubu, Khamis Musa Darazo, has urged the Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies to scrutinise recent statements attributed to former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye, concerning the 2027 general elections. Darazo, who made the call while speaking with journalists in Bauchi on Thursday, said the move was necessary to safeguard national security and prevent political utterances capable of heightening tension or creating unnecessary apprehension among Nigerians. He, however, cautioned that his call should not be interpreted as an attempt to intimidate opposition politicians or suppress democratic freedoms, stressing that democracy accommodates criticism, disagreement and healthy political competition. According to him, political leaders must recognise the responsibility that comes with public statements, particularly as the country approaches another election cycle. “This is not about persecution, intimidation or silencing the opposition. It is about responsibility. If a statement made by a prominent political actor has generated legitimate security concerns, the authorities have every right to seek clarification and establish the facts,” he said. Darazo maintained that security agencies must apply the law fairly, irrespective of political affiliation, warning against the use of national security as a partisan instrument. He also urged Melaye and other political leaders to exercise restraint in their public statements, saying Nigeria could not afford another atmosphere of political tension, fear and confrontation ahead of the 2027 elections. “Political disagreement is normal in a democracy. What is unacceptable is allowing political competition to gradually become a source of tension among citizens. We should sell our ideas, present our records and persuade Nigerians rather than create unnecessary anxiety,” he added. The APC chieftain challenged opposition politicians to focus their campaigns on policies, programmes, leadership capacity and verifiable records rather than provocative statements capable of distracting attention from issues affecting Nigerians. He said supporters of President Tinubu were prepared for the 2027 political contest and would continue to defend the administration based on its policies, achievements and Renewed Hope Agenda. “We are not afraid of opposition. We welcome competition. But competition must be democratic, peaceful and issue-based. President Tinubu will be judged by Nigerians based on his record, just as every opposition politician will be judged by the people based on what they offer,” Darazo said. He called on the DSS and other relevant security institutions to remain professional, impartial and guided by the law in handling politically sensitive matters. He further urged political actors across party lines to place the country’s peace, unity and democratic stability above personal and par

item.title: 2027: S’west monarchs back southern presidency, endorse Tinubu, support state police
item.description: …reject fuel subsidy return, urge peaceful elections, commend new military formations in Oyo, Ekiti By Adeola Badru Traditional rulers from across the South-West have endorsed the continuation of the presidency in Southern Nigeria beyond the 2027 general elections, declaring that sustaining the principle of power rotation is critical to national unity, political stability, equity and inclusiveness. The monarchs also reaffirmed their unwavering support for President Bola Tinubu and his administration while backing the proposed establishment of state police as part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture. These were among the major resolutions reached at a meeting of the South-West Council of Obas and Traditional Rulers held at the Aafin Olubadan, Oke Aremo, Ibadan, Oyo State, on Wednesday. The meeting, which brought together prominent traditional rulers from the six South-West states, also endorsed the Federal Government’s position against the reintroduction of fuel subsidy, called for peaceful and credible elections in 2027, and urged greater collaboration among Nigeria’s geopolitical regions. In a communiqué issued and read by the Alake of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Gbadebo, at the end of the meeting, said the rotational presidency arrangement had contributed significantly to political stability, inclusiveness and national cohesion, stressing that the arrangement should be sustained in the next electoral cycle. The Council declared, “The principle of rotational presidency has, over the years, contributed significantly to political stability, inclusiveness, and national cohesion across Nigeria.” “In the interest of fairness, equity, and the continued strengthening of national unity, the Council expressed the view that the rotational arrangement should be sustained and that the presidency should remain in Southern Nigeria in the next electoral cycle, in line with the spirit of power rotation that has helped preserve peace and stability in the country.” The monarchs explained that their position was informed by the need to strengthen mutual trust among the federating units and preserve the delicate balance required for the country’s continued progress. They added that the position was intended to promote “national balance, mutual trust among the federating units, and the continued progress of the Nigerian State”. On the 2027 general elections, the traditional rulers called on political parties, candidates and the electorate to embrace democratic values and shun activities capable of undermining the electoral process. They condemned electoral violence, intimidation, vote-buying and other forms of electoral malpractice, emphasising the need for peaceful, free and credible elections at all levels. “The Council underscored the importance of peaceful, free, and credible elections at all levels. item.title: Manchester United ‘Reach Verbal Agreement’ With Ex-Chelsea Coach Pochettino To Replace Carrick
item.description: Manchester United have reportedly reached a “verbal agreement in principle” with Argentine Mauricio Pochettino to replace embattled Michael Carrick as their manager in a bid to revive the fortunes of the struggling English giants. Carrick’s position at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. He remains in post, but it is believed Carrick’s future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday. Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United States head coach Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. It was only three months ago, however, that Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup. US Soccer would be due compensation should he move to Manchester, with the 54-year-old understood to have a $10 million (£7.5 million) release clause. But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have “reached a verbal agreement in principle” with Pochettino, linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach. Turbulent Reign Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training ground on Wednesday, but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. Manchester United’s English head coach Michael Carrick reacts on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge in London on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) The 45-year-old had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. But United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It appeared former United and England midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed Aston Villa by two goals on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But a change now appears likely, with former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann also linked with the United job. item.title: VIDEO: Tinubu Receives Flamingos In Abuja After World Cup Victory
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has received the Flamingos after winning Africa’s first-ever U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, received the victorious players and technical crew on behalf of the President at the Presidential Banquet Hall, Abuja. ﻿ The U-17 team won their first FIFA World Cup title after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. The Flamingos lost their opener 2-1 to Poland, but dominated in the remaining matches, defeating defending champions North Korea, Puerto Rico, and Mexico. Their first-ever appearance in the final was sealed with a 3-1 victory over Brazil, before taking home the trophy after beating Japan. Flamingos celebrating their U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup The players have received commendations from government officials and football fans around the world. President Tinubu congratulated the Flamingos for becoming the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, said he received the news upon his return from campaign engagements in Akwa Ibom and Rivers States. He also described Nigeria’s maiden triumph as a proud moment for the country and a landmark achievement for African women’s football. The Senate also pledged a ₦100 million reward for the Flamingos. The pledge followed a motion moved by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Sports, Senator Abdul Ningi, who congratulated the players on their outstanding performance and commended the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) for its role in the team’s achievement. The latest feat by a Nigerian sports team came less than two years after the senior women’s football team, Super Falcons, won their 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in Morocco. item.title: Many terrorists neutralised as military sustains pressure on enclaves
item.description: Scores of terrorists have been neutralised across different communities in the Northern region of the country following the pressure sustained in their enclaves by the troops of the Nigerian military. The troops, in different operations sustained pressure on the criminals and dismantled criminal networks with a view to protecting lives and property, and restoring lasting peace and security across the country. Daily Trust reports that the development was in line with the commitment of the Armed Forces of Nigeria under the leadership of General Olufemi Olatunbosun Oluyede. The four-star general, has at different fora maintained that he would continue to ensure that all law-abiding Nigerians, particularly those in the Northern Nigeria sleep with their two eyes closed. Updating Nigerians on the efforts being made to restore peace across the country, the Director, Defence Media Operations, Major-General Michael Onoja disclosed that consistent efforts were made to deny terrorists, kidnappers, gunrunners and other criminal groups’ freedom of action between October 30th and November 5th, 2026. Terrorists suffer heavy losses in Northeast Checks showed that in the North East geopolitical zone, troops of Operation HADIN KAI inflicted heavy losses on terrorists who attempted to strike at troops’ locations in Borno and Yobe States. Subsequently, troops pressed home the advantage with clearance operations and a wave of arrests. On the night of October 29th, 2026, terrorists approached Buni Yadi in Gujba LGA of Yobe State, from the Timbuktu Triangle axis. However, troops countered the attack and subsequent exploitation on 30 October 30th, 2026 discovered the bodies of 48 terrorists, along with 42 AK-47 rifles, five PKT machine guns, four general-purpose machine guns, a 60mm mortar, 105 magazines and two video cameras. The following day, troops’ operations around Apama and Jauro Bashir along the terrorists’ withdrawal route, recovered three corpses, an AK-47 rifle and 188 rounds of ammunition. The senior military officer confirmed that on the same day, terrorists also attempted to infiltrate a troops’ location at Bitta in Gwoza LGA of Borno State but were forced to retreat. He added, “Exploitation at first light recovered the bodies of seven terrorists, four AK-47 rifles, an RPG tube, four RPG bombs, three RPG chargers, a PKM machine gun and a radio. “Troops also received several surrendered members of terrorist groups, rescued escapees and dismantled terrorist support networks across the theatre. “Between 2 – 4 November 2026, twelve terrorist fighters and family members surrendered at New Abaram Resettlement Village and Banki Junction in Bama LGA and near Ngurusoye in Gwoza LGA in Borno State.” On November 2nd, 2026, troops rescued a female abductee who had escaped from the Mandara Mountains at Hudugum, Hambagda, along the Gwoza-Limankara Road.
